newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore election to be held after Jan 5, 1997-PM.
newsitem.headline: Singapore election to be held after Jan 5, 1997-PM.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said on Sunday the next general election would be held after January 5, 1997, state television reported.
It also quoted Goh as saying he planned to serve out his full term of parliament, which ends in January.
Under Singapore's constitution, Goh can call elections for any time up to three months after his five-year elected term ends, it said.
Goh did not give a date for the elections but he has said previously he favoured either February or March 1997.
Goh's People's Action Party took around 60 percent of the vote and all but four of the 81 seats in Singapore's parliament in the last polls in 1991.

Local newspapers on Sunday had earlier quoted Goh as ridiculing speculation that he had merely been standing in as leader since 1990 while Lee Hsien Loong, son of Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew, was groomed for the job.
"When I first took over, I remember people touting me as a seat-warmer," Goh was quoted by the Sunday Times newspaper as telling a meeting of PAP activists on Saturday night.

"I think I can qualify as the longest seat-warmer in history. In the coming election, if you signal that you want me to continue, I shall leave the seat so warm that my successor will have to find a new chair," he said.
